newsitem.title: UK: European markets rise despite U.S. rate fears.
newsitem.headline: European markets rise despite U.S. rate fears.

text.p: European stocks and bonds followed Wall Street's lead and rallied on Tuesday after investors appeared to accept the idea that U.S. interest rates were set to rise for the first time in more than two years.
All three of Europe's major bourses -- London, Paris and Frankfurt -- rose in morning trading.
On the foreign exchange market the dollar firmed against the yen and mark, although movements were small ahead of a policy-making meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve.

German government bonds also firmed with British bonds or gilts, taking their cue from a rally in U.S. Treasury bonds overnight after the market factored in an expected 0.25 percentage point rise in U.S. rates.
"A quarter-point rate rise is fully discounted now," said Norman Beauchamp, head of derivatives at the Cooperative Bank.

The market focus was firmly turned towards Washington where the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) was due to announce the result of its deliberations after 1900 GMT -- well after the close of European markets.
With financial markets already primed for a quarter point rate increase, analysts said investors were now looking at the prospects for continuing U.S. economic expansion.
As a result, the Dow Jones industrial average of blue chip shares, which was down 17 points as London markets closed on Monday, rebounded to close up 100.46 points or 1.48 percent.
Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan laid the groundwork last week for a possible rise by stressing the importance to the economy of keeping inflation down.
But until a decision emerges from the FOMC, one London dealer said he expected European markets to remain cautious.
"There just wasn't much meat in the Dow's rally yesterday," said Kirit Shah, strategist at Sanwa International in London. "I I can't see the Dow being able to sustain any move above the 7,000 level."

Should the FOMC decide to raise rates by half a percentage point, share markets are likely to fall on both sides of the Atlantic. No rate increase could spark an initial, but short-lived rally, analysts said.
London blue chips, which fell 4.7 percent during the six sessions up until Monday, rebounded during the morning by more than one percent.

Among individual stocks, shares in Abbey National Plc rose 12.5p to 727 as bank stocks rallied from recent weakness and the market welcomed Abbey's failure to win control of insurer Scottish Amicable. Prudential Corp, confirmed as the winning bidder, rose 17p to 556 after being seen deriving strategic and earnings benefits from the deal
Shares in British Steel bucked the firmer market trend, sinking five pence to 156.5 after news that Germany's Krupp was calling off its bid for Thyssen.
The shares of both German companies fell in Frankfurt trading, Krupp dropping 3.5 marks to 335 but well off its lows, while Thyssen plunged 40 marks to 377.5.
The blue chip DAX-30 index rose 25.6 points to 3,347.44 by 1215 GMT, but traders said turnover was low ahead of the FOMC.
French shares opened similarly higher, the CAC-40 index standing 22 points up at mid-session but down from its best.
Lyonnaise des Eauxand Cie de Suez were strong on the back of an expected share swap bid of two Suez shares for one Lyonnaise share as part of a friendly merger.

On the foreign exchange market, the dollar started in Europe on a firm note. By 1215 GMT the currency was standing at 1.6870 marks and 123.52 yen compared with 1.6874 marks and 122.85 yen in late trading on Monday.
With the market having priced in a 25-basis-point hike in the key Federal funds rate, there was little the dollar could do until the central bank actually made a move, traders said.
CURRENCIES AT 1215 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6870 marks and 123.52 yen compared with 1.6874 and 122.85 in late trade on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1215 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 43.7 points, or 1.04 percent, at 4,258.5.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 22.05 points, or 0.85 percent, at 2,601.33.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 25.6 points, or 0.77 percent, at 3,347.44.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $350.90 an ounce versus $350.20 on Monday afternoon. Silver was four cents higher at $5.18.
